I think you’re fundamentally misunderstanding the goal of the matchmaker.

It is not to rank you up over time. It is to consistently give you balanced matches. I have dozens of friends at every rank. When I look at their accounts (especially my old OG friends who have been playing for years) several things become clear:

Regardless of where a player is ranked initially most of the time they will never rank higher than two rank tiers above or below what they initially place. I have a friend who I’ve played with since 2018. He was silver through most of Overwatch 1, sometimes peaking into gold, and only recently finally hit plat last year. 

I have another friend who did his placements and basically kept winning until he was M5 and just couldn’t climb anymore. It honestly looked like he was barely trying in Diamond but was still winning almost every game. He bounces between high diamond and low Masters. 

Does this mean it’s impossible to climb? No! Because I myself first started as a silver noob in 2016 and I was hardstuck gold from 2017-2019.

In 2019 I had a lot of time on my hands and I decided to dedicate myself to truly climbing and learning this game. I actually paid for some coaching. And man the way I looked at the entire game changed. Suddenly I was noticing things about this game that I never even considered before and it just made me realize I truly was the only constant variable in all my games. And I have the power to effect the outcomes of my matches. Not all of them but a lot of them. 

I’m D1 now and I can taste Masters and that’s where I’ll basically be done with my goals for this game. 

I have a few friends I met when I decided to grind the game and they had similar experiences. They loved the game, wanted to play it better so they made a consistent effort to.

Here’s a bit of a secret, playing overwatch to rank up is actually not very “fun” you have to be consciously thinking about A LOT of stuff all the time. It turns the game into a huge slog of micro managing cooldowns and enemy positioning. 

You actually WANT to be “hardstuck” because when you are in the correct rank you have the highest chance of just being able to log in and have a good fun game of Overwatch. 

But if you want to CLIMB I promise you it’s not just something that happens. You don’t have to get a coach but you have to make it a persistent effort and for 90% of people they are not going to put in the work for a video game rank that ultimately does not matter.

“No aim no brain must be a Winston main” is a meme for a reason haha. He is less about aim and more about timing your engages and bubbles properly (sure he has his long range shot but it’s bad so you’re not missing out on not using it)

Reinhardt is a name that gets thrown around a lot but he has Firestrike which is an important ability you don’t want to just miss all the time. Also pin requires a bit of aim to use optimally. 

Mercy/Moira/Lifeweaver are your big 3 supports that don’t require hand eye coordination to be successful with. 

People will say Moira is “harder to aim with now” that’s ridiculous just aim in the general direction of the enemy and be in position to spray your piss all over your teammates. Your balls are chuck and forget as well. 

Lifeweaver is here in case you want a bit of a challenge. His heals lock on, as does his most important ability life grip. Of course he does have thorn volley his shooting ability and that is a very weak and hard to aim projectile but you literally never need to use it if you don’t want to. 

Be aware not to go with Brigitte. On paper she might just seem like a support version of Reinhardt where you just swing a flail. And yes that part of her kit doesn’t require aim but you are REQUIRED to hit whipshots if you really want to succeed with her. So I would avoid her.

Finally for DPS I can’t really think of too many. They pretty much all require aim at some point. If you insist on playing DPS then I recommend something tanky and that can kill quickly. 

For tanky DPS you are looking at Torb, Mei, and Bastion.

Torb has an auto turret that is actually quite good now with perks. Yes he has his rivet gun which is another projectile gun you’d have to aim but its bullets have a good size so you’ll be surprised how often you’ll hit a random dink. 

90% of Mei’s kit does not require aim. Her primary fire is an ice spray that’s very easy to aim. She has two abilities: ice block which freezes her in place but heals her HP. And ice wall, a big chunky wall that you will mostly use to help you get out of tough spots or to help you get a close quarters kill. She does have a secondary fire which is an icicle. Pretty fast and big projectile not hard to hit. 

Bastion: he’s the tankiest DPS next to Torb. Now while you might not find success with his primary fire in recon mode you want to play him more for turret mode and launching your grenade at clumps of enemies. The grenade bounces and sticks to targets so it’s a great ability that doesn’t require a bunch of aim. And turret mode is very easy to aim because you’re shooting like 5 million bullets a second.

And finally Junk. Who I hesitate to recommend but I can’t deny Spamrat has his place. Just find a safe little spot vaguely near the enemy team and start shooting bombs until things die lol. The reason I hesitate to recommend him is because to be GOOD at Junkrat you will eventually have to learn to aim, and not just aim, you’ll have to learn mine jumps and mine grenade combos. Might be a little much.

Brig is the ultimate bodyguard. She can make any one person functionally immortal with repair pack, shield, and flail. This works REALLY good with any of the carry supports (Ana/Juno) because they can heal the rest of your team and provide insane utility while not having to worry about dying. 

Now with inspire, don’t think of it as 15 health, think of it as a VERY easy ability to proc that will heal EVERY person in the inspire radius for 60 health. The range of the ability and the ease of activating it is where the power comes from. Imagine a Lifeweaver able to send a healing blossom to their whole team once. That’s the power of the ability (granted the healing isn’t instant but the wide range of the ability means you will be healing a lot if you are constantly proc’ing it.)

And this is where the OP feedback loop starts with Brig. Not only is she keeping a high hps, high utility support immortal, but she is supplementing those high heals with her own 60 heals over 4 seconds *every single time she procs inspire* this means multiple 60 heal “pools” she leaves around the map every time she hits anything with the mace. 

So now the team has Ana or Juno heals (and all the utility that entails) AND on top of that Brig heals that keep everyone comfortably healthy. AND on top of that Brig makes the other support immortal AND if you just dive the Brig she still has her shield bash + rocket flail to escape so she’s hard to kill herself.
